batch_strategy: Freeze these 32 distinct supplied candidate IDs with their supplied premeasurement predictions. Target unresolved structure-condition relationships through matched loading contrasts, missing solvent-ratio transitions, selected strong-eluent endpoints, and one deliberate repeat. Observed evidence IDs appear only in the hypotheses' typed evidence lists.

choices.reason: m120 at 1/1 and 50 uL establishes the low-loading baseline before its measured 2/1 and 5/1 responses. Comparison with the measured 150 uL condition at 1/1 tests whether the pronounced loading association begins before the sharp low-loading retention rise.

m75 at 10/1 and 50 uL bridges matched-loading measurements at 5/1, 20/1, and 50/1. The unexpectedly early recent 50/1 measurement makes it useful to locate the preceding rise and test the predicted curve without imposing a monotonic diester response.

m186 at 0/1 and 100 uL fills the loading midpoint between measurements of 31.65/31.72 mL at 50 uL and 4.31/13.99 mL at 150 uL. This tests an intermediate loading-associated response versus an isolated unusual low-loading record; the current 13.28/22.70 mL prediction remains untested.

m118 at 10/1 and 100 uL bridges its same-loading 5/1 and much later 50/1 measurements. The latter exposed substantial historical underprediction. This point localizes response curvature for para-anisaldehyde instead of applying a common upward shift to its entire curve.

m118 at 20/1 and 50 uL supplies another transition point alongside the selected 10/1 experiment. Its predicted 34.65/66.21 mL response tests where the strong growth measured at 50/1 develops. Loading differs from the 100 uL anchors and will remain explicit in interpreting the result.

m78 at 20/1 and 100 uL completes a matched-loading bridge between measured 10/1 and 50/1 conditions. Recent overprediction at 5/1 and underprediction at 50/1 show that learning this keto ester's curve shape is more useful than a constant correction.

m127 at 50/1 and 100 uL tests whether the predicted onset growth persists after the recent 10/1 measurement started at only 5.47 mL. The current 21.85/55.69 mL prediction could represent genuine later growth or excessive transfer from other methoxy carbonyls.

m195 at 20/1 and 100 uL probes a predicted onset maximum near 23.86 mL. Its measured 150 uL condition at this ratio has nearly coincident, slightly inverted endpoints, while the measured 50/1 condition at 100 uL starts earlier. This checks whether the apparent reversal extends beyond that unusual record.

m125 at 1/1, 50 uL sample, and 300 uL DCM directly contrasts with an existing 500 uL DCM measurement. Together with the selected 100 uL sample contrast, it tests loading-solvent-volume dependence at two sample masses where current predictions barely distinguish 300 from 500 uL.

m125 at 1/1, 100 uL sample, and 500 uL DCM contrasts directly with its measured 300 uL DCM condition. Existing 2/1 volume contrasts differ strongly in completion. This paired design tests transfer to 1/1 while retaining record variability as an alternative explanation.

m96 at 20/1 and 150 uL bridges its measured 5/1 condition at the same loading and its 50/1 condition at 100 uL. The recent 50/1 acquisition underpredicted onset more than completion. This tests endpoint-specific growth for a thiol-containing ester while preserving the loading distinction.

m208 at 5/1 and 50 uL tests an unusually early prediction of 2.04/8.11 mL. Measured 20/1 and 50/1 conditions are much later but do not establish the early curve. Pairing this with 2/1 at the same loading directly tests the predicted reversal.

m67 at 20/1 and 100 uL extends a secondary benzylic-alcohol response beyond measured 5/1 and 10/1 conditions. Its near-maximum supplied CW distance supports investigating this uncovered condition. The label constrains donor-family curvature without assuming that m120's unusual loading behavior transfers.

m207 at 5/1 and 50 uL supplies a direct loading contrast to the short measured 100 uL response. This molecule becomes much later at 10/1. Testing whether its early 5/1 regime survives lower loading provides a useful structural comparison to m120's recent loading association.

m119 at 2/1 and 100 uL places an intermediate anchor before its late measured 5/1 response at the same loading. Methoxyphenethyl alcohol differs from methoxybenzyl alcohol m120 in hydroxyl placement. This tests structural transfer of a retention transition beyond shared donor and acceptor counts.

m119 at 5/1 and 150 uL directly contrasts with its measured 100 uL condition. The current prediction remains near 48.74/77.07 mL despite the mass change. This tests whether the severe loading association found for m120 also occurs in its phenethyl-alcohol relative.

m44 at 0/1 and 50 uL starts a matched loading contrast for ortho-methylacetophenone. Related dimethyl compound m33 shows measured completion growth with loading, whereas the more methylated m29 recently had a short pure-EA interval. This tests the structural specificity of that tail behavior.

m44 at 0/1 and 150 uL completes the selected 50-to-150 uL contrast. The two predictions are almost identical despite m33's measured loading-associated completion growth. These labels can teach whether removing one ring methyl changes loading-dependent interval shape.

m81 at 0/1 and 100 uL adds an unmeasured strong-eluent loading beside the short measured 150 uL endpoint. Recent 1/1 measurements at 50 and 150 uL have similar onsets but completion volumes of 13.71 and 6.66 mL. This tests whether a loading-associated tail difference persists at stronger eluent.

m80 at 20/1 and 100 uL tests an uncovered intermediate-ratio regime where predicted endpoints are nearly coincident and slightly reversed. Short measured 50/1 intervals provide anchors. This constrains diester response after m75's surprising recent result without treating either diester as a universal template.

m19 at 2/1 and 100 uL fills the loading midpoint between measured 50 and 150 uL conditions. Their onsets differ by about 10.3 mL while completion is nearly unchanged. This directly tests whether loading can influence onset separately from completion.

m72 at 5/1 and 50 uL with PE/300 uL loading pairs with the selected DCM/200 uL condition at equal sample mass. Measured 20/1 conditions differ in onset under these loading packages. This tests whether the difference appears already at 5/1; solvent identity and loading volume remain coupled.

m72 at 5/1 and 50 uL with DCM/200 uL loading completes the matched-mass loading-package comparison. It also contrasts with an existing 150 uL DCM measurement. The nearly equal package predictions can therefore be tested against both loading amount and ratio-dependent package effects.

m194 at 2/1 and 150 uL follows its same-loading 1/1 measurement of 4.59/27.33 mL. The model predicts a shorter completion volume near 20.77 mL at 2/1. This tests the predicted dip while holding loading fixed, with a measured 5/1 condition providing a different-loading reference.

m25 at 5/1 and 100 uL fills a missing part of the tert-butyl keto-ester curve between measured 2/1 and 10/1 regions. Comparison with m82, m95, m78, and m81 can teach substituent-dependent beta-keto-ester responses, whose measured interval shapes and historical errors differ substantially.

m13 at 5/1 and 100 uL fills the loading midpoint between measured 50 and 150 uL conditions. Their onsets decrease from 23.90 to 17.85 mL while completion stays around 40–44 mL. Alongside the accurate recent 2/1 bridge, this tests loading effects near a retention transition.

m62 at 10/1 and 150 uL checks the same mass as its unusually narrow measured 5/1 interval. Recent 5/1 labels at lower loadings were much earlier. A new ratio at 150 uL tests whether the late onset persists across conditions or is confined to the exceptional 5/1 record.

Repeat m73 at 1/1 and 50 uL, where a previous measurement showed a delayed, narrow interval. Two 100 uL records disagree strongly despite nearly identical recorded densities. This repeat tests reproducibility after the m80 repeat demonstrated substantial within-tuple completion variation.

m45 at 10/1 and 100 uL adds a missing loading level beside its measured 50 uL condition. The measured 20/1 series shows a strong loading-associated onset decrease. This tests transfer of that association to 10/1, away from the unphysical 50/1 record.

m36 at 0/1 and 50 uL extends the matched-loading curve backward from measured 1/1 and 2/1 conditions. Its current early 4.95/14.96 mL prediction tests where aminoacetophenone loses its delayed onset under stronger eluent, constraining topology-specific nitrogen response.

m198 at 50/1 and 100 uL extends ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde beyond measured 20/1 and 5/1 conditions. Its predicted 33.67/78.37 mL response tests high-ratio transfer after m118's large historical underprediction. Para-nitro observations provide a distinct positional-topology reference.

m208 at 2/1 and 50 uL supplies the matched-loading lower-ratio point for the selected 5/1 experiment. Predictions decrease from 4.06/11.34 to 2.04/8.11 mL as PE increases. The paired labels test this reversal and connect the early curve to measured late-retention conditions.

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing molecules have topology-specific ratio transitions and loading-associated endpoint responses. In m19, loading is associated primarily with onset at 2/1; m72 also shows differences between recorded loading packages at 20/1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These observations motivate interactions between nitrogen environment, ratio, and recorded loading conditions, with separate responses for onset and completion. The PE/DCM comparison also changes loading-solvent volume, so it cannot identify a solvent-only mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m19 midpoint follow its loading-associated onset trend, does the m72 loading-package difference emerge at 5/1, and where does the m36 onset transition begin?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl-family response curvature and interval shape require motif-specific learning. Recent labels show opposing historical errors across m78, m118, m75, and m127, making a common retention shift inappropriate.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Ratio bridges and structural contrasts can teach when onset rises, when only completion expands, and when a predicted continuation fails. Acquisition-time errors identify historical failure regions but are not current-model residuals.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do missing m118 and m78 points locate smooth or sharp transitions, and do m75, m127, m194, and the selected ester and sulfur environments follow their currently predicted curve shapes?

hypotheses.content: Recent outcomes support overgeneralization as an explanation for several predicted 0/1 onset spikes. Completion under pure EA can remain broad, and the late-onset m186 50 uL record remains an isolated exception requiring local investigation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The hydroxyaldehyde and neutral-control labels weaken a shared late-onset interpretation. Separate endpoint learning remains essential because m197 still finishes much later than neutral controls despite its early onset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m186 at 100 uL interpolate between its two different 0/1 loading endpoints, or join the early-onset responses measured for other hydroxyaldehydes?

hypotheses.content: Selected molecules show ratio-dependent and endpoint-specific loading associations that nearly invariant predictions may miss. Their direction is not universal, and recorded-condition variability remains a competing explanation for some contrasts.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: m120's low-loading retention, m33's completion growth, and m81's opposite completion association should not be averaged into one mass correction. Matched contrasts can make the density-times-volume feature informative while testing transfer across structures and ratios.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which loading associations persist at another ratio or in a structural relative, and which disappear when another loading level is measured?

hypotheses.content: Identical recorded tuples can have substantially different labels, and isolated nearly coincident or inverted endpoints should not automatically define a general adsorption response.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m80 repeat weakens interpretation of its original middle-loading tail as reproducible. A targeted m73 repeat and extensions near m195 and m62 can limit propagation from unusual records. Missing explanatory variables cannot be identified from this catalog.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m73 repeat reproduce its delayed narrow interval, and do nearby m195 and m62 conditions reproduce their unusual onset behavior?

hypotheses.content: For m125, larger DCM loading volume may affect completion in a ratio-dependent way that the predictor largely ignores; record variability remains a competing explanation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: At 2/1, matched-mass 300/500 uL records differ strongly in completion, whereas the 150 uL sample pair at 5/1 has similar completion. This motivates testing interactions rather than a universal volume shift. The selected 1/1 contrasts compare loading volume at two sample masses using existing anchors.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 1/1, do the two matched loading-volume contrasts show a coherent completion difference, or further favor record variability over a transferable volume response?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes strengthened the overgeneralization explanation for the previous 0/1 hypothesis: m117, m190, m197, and high-loading m186 all started near 4–5 mL despite much later predicted onsets. However, m197 retained a broad completion tail, so a blanket downward correction to both endpoints would also fail. The m186 midpoint is now more informative than another cross-scaffold onset-spike probe. Carbonyl feedback remained bidirectional: m78 and m118 at 50/1 were substantially later than predicted, while m75 at 50/1 and m127 at 10/1 were earlier. This increases the value of missing response-curve points and topology-specific transfer. The m120 outcomes exposed a stronger loading association than anticipated: low-loading 5/1 was late, whereas high-loading 2/1 was short. I therefore test its low-loading baseline and alcohol relatives rather than treating its earlier apparent ratio reversal as established. m33's new midpoint supports loading-associated completion growth, while m81 shows the opposite association at 1/1. Finally, the m80 repeat finished at 7.31 mL rather than the original 15.66 mL at the same recorded tuple, weakening the proposed reproducible middle-loading tail. The new m62 labels likewise do not establish a smooth loading response toward its unusual 150 uL record. These outcomes favor localized checks and limit mechanistic claims from exceptional intervals.
batch_rationale: The 32 experiments combine failure repair with interpretable condition exploration. Ratio bridges for m118, m78, m75, m127, m194, m96, and m198 address curve shapes that recent measurements showed cannot share one correction. The m208 pair tests a conspicuous predicted reversal using equal loading, while m67 and m119 extend donor response curves with measured anchors. Loading experiments around m120, m44, m81, m19, m13, and m45 test whether onset and completion respond differently, including transfer to related structures. The m125 design specifically tests loading-solvent volume, and the m72 pair tests a coupled solvent/volume package without claiming to isolate its components. One deliberate m73 repeat, together with extensions near m186, m195, and m62, addresses the demonstrated risk of propagating isolated unusual labels. Multiple rows for a molecule serve explicit contrasts. Supplied CW distances and quantile spreads support exploration of some transition regions but are not calibrated epistemic uncertainty; quantile crossings also do not establish a measured error. V2 minus V1 remains the physical elution interval. Retraining on these labels may improve Row-distribution accuracy by teaching when structural corrections transfer, where ratio responses change shape, how loading conditions affect each endpoint, and where the recorded variables leave substantial conditional variation.
